title.zh: 卷五十一 志第四十一 食貨一
title.raw: 卷五十一 志第四十一 食貨一 Volume 51 Treatises 47: Finance and Economics 1

sentences.zh: 食貨一

translations.literal: Finance and Economics 1
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics 1

sentences.zh: 古之善治其國而愛養斯民者，必立經常簡易之法，使上愛物以養其下，下勉力以事其上，上足而下不困。

translations.literal: In antiquity, those who governed their states well and cherished and nurtured the people invariably established regular, simple laws, so that above they cherished goods to nourish those below, below they strove to serve those above, above had enough and below were not distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who truly governed well in antiquity always set up steady, straightforward institutions: the ruler valued resources to support the people, the people labored to serve the throne, the court was supplied and the common folk were not squeezed dry.

sentences.zh: 故量人之力而授之田，量地之產而取以給公上，量其入而出之以為用度之數。

translations.literal: Therefore they measured men's strength and granted them fields, measured the land's yield and took from it to supply the public above, measured revenue and disbursed it as the figure for expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: They matched each person's capacity when allotting land, took from the soil only what was needed for public revenue, and scaled spending to what came in.

sentences.zh: 是三者常相須以濟而不可失，失其一則不能守其二。

translations.literal: These three constantly depended on one another to succeed and could not be lost; lose one and the other two could not be maintained.
translations.idiomatic: The three measures had to work together; lose any one and the other two would collapse.

sentences.zh: 及暴君庸主，縱其佚欲，而茍且之吏從之，變制合時以取寵於其上。

translations.literal: When tyrannical rulers and mediocre lords indulged their excess desires, opportunist officials followed them, altering institutions to suit the moment in order to win favor from above.
translations.idiomatic: Tyrants and weak sovereigns gave free rein to luxury, and servile officials rewrote the rules on the fly to please them.

sentences.zh: 故用於上者無節，而取於下者無限，民竭其力而不能供，由是上愈不足而下愈困，則財利之說興，而聚斂之臣用。

translations.literal: Thus what was used above had no limit, while what was taken from below had no bound; the people exhausted their strength yet could not supply it—whereupon above grew ever more insufficient and below ever more distressed, and then doctrines of profit arose and ministers of exaction were employed.
translations.idiomatic: Court spending knew no restraint and extraction from the people knew no ceiling; the folk spent themselves dry yet still could not pay. The treasury grew emptier while the countryside grew poorer, profit-seeking policies flourished, and revenue-hungry ministers took charge.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「寧畜盜臣。

translations.literal: The Record says: "Better keep a thieving minister."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "It is better to harbor a thieving minister."

sentences.zh: 」盜臣誠可惡，然一人之害爾。

translations.literal: A thieving minister is indeed detestable, yet the harm is only that of one man.
translations.idiomatic: A corrupt official is hateful enough, but he injures only himself.

sentences.zh: 聚斂之臣用，則經常之法壞，而下不勝其弊焉。

translations.literal: When ministers of exaction are employed, the regular laws are destroyed, and those below cannot bear the harm.
translations.idiomatic: When exaction specialists rule, the standing order is ruined and the people cannot survive the damage.

sentences.zh: 唐之始時，授人以口分、世業田，而取之以租、庸、調之法，其用之也有節。

translations.literal: At the Tang's beginning, men were granted koufen and shiye fields, and taxes were taken by the zu, yong, and diao method; expenditures were also restrained.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang was founded, the state allotted per-capita and hereditary fields and collected zu, yong, and diao levies—and spending stayed within bounds.

sentences.zh: 蓋其畜兵以府衛之制，故兵雖多而無所損；

translations.literal: For they maintained troops by the fubing and guard-garrison system, so though troops were many there was no drain;
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers were raised through the fubing militia and guard-garrison system, so a large army did not bankrupt the realm;

sentences.zh: 設官有常員之數，故官不濫而易祿。

translations.literal: offices were established with fixed quotas, so offices were not excessive and salaries were easy to pay.
translations.idiomatic: each post had a fixed headcount, so offices were not overfilled and salaries remained payable.

sentences.zh: 雖不及三代之盛時，然亦可以為經常之法也。

translations.literal: Though it did not match the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties, it could still serve as regular law.
translations.idiomatic: It fell short of the golden ages of antiquity, yet it could still stand as a durable fiscal order.

sentences.zh: 及其弊也，兵冗官濫，為之大蠹。

translations.literal: When it declined, redundant troops and excessive offices became a great plague.
translations.idiomatic: In time the system rotted: bloated armies and swollen bureaucracy became its gravest blight.

sentences.zh: 自天寶以來，大盜屢起，方鎮數叛，兵革之興，累世不息，而用度之數，不能節矣。

translations.literal: From the Tianbao era onward, great bandits arose repeatedly, regional commanders rebelled again and again, warfare flared generation after generation without cease, and the figures for expenditure could no longer be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianbao years, major rebellions broke out again and again, frontier governors turned traitor one after another, and war ran on for generations. The budget could no longer be held in check.

sentences.zh: 加以驕君昏主，奸吏邪臣，取濟一時，屢更其制，而經常之法，蕩然盡矣。

translations.literal: Added to this were arrogant rulers and benighted sovereigns, corrupt officials and wicked ministers, seeking temporary relief and repeatedly changing the system until the regular laws were utterly swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant emperors and muddled courts, venal clerks and scheming ministers patched crises with stopgaps, rewrote the rules again and again, and the standing order vanished entirely.

sentences.zh: 由是財利之說興，聚斂之臣進。

translations.literal: Hence doctrines of profit arose and ministers of exaction advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Profit-seeking theories spread, and men who lived to squeeze revenue rose to power.

sentences.zh: 蓋口分、世業之田壞而為兼並，租、庸、調之法壞而為兩稅。

translations.literal: The koufen and shiye fields were destroyed and became consolidated holdings; the zu, yong, and diao system was destroyed and became the dual tax.
translations.idiomatic: Per-capita and hereditary allotments collapsed into large estates; the zu-yong-diao levies gave way to the dual tax.

sentences.zh: 至於鹽鐵、轉運、屯田、和糴、鑄錢、括苗、榷利、借商、進奉、獻助，無所不為矣。

translations.literal: As for salt and iron monopolies, transport commissions, garrison farming, government grain purchases, coinage, land surveys, state monopolies, loans to merchants, tribute deliveries, and voluntary contributions—nothing was left undone.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and iron monopolies, transport offices, military farms, forced purchases of grain, minting, land surveys, excise levies, loans to merchants, court tribute, and "voluntary" gifts—every expedient was tried.

sentences.zh: 蓋愈煩而愈弊，以至於亡焉。

translations.literal: The more elaborate it grew, the more corrupt it became, until the dynasty perished.
translations.idiomatic: The more tangled the system grew, the worse it failed—until the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 唐制：度田以步，其闊一步，其長二百四十步為畝，百畝為頃。

translations.literal: Tang regulation: fields were measured in paces; one pace wide and two hundred forty paces long made one mu; one hundred mu made one qing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang law, land was measured in paces: one pace in width and two hundred forty in length formed one mu; one hundred mu made one qing.

sentences.zh: 凡民始生為黃，四歲為小，十六為中，二十一為丁，六十為老。

translations.literal: All commoners at birth were classified huang; at four years, xiao; at sixteen, zhong; at twenty-one, ding; at sixty, lao.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners were registered at birth as infants (huang), as minors at four, as youths at sixteen, as adult males (ding) at twenty-one, and as elderly at sixty.

sentences.zh: 授田之制，丁及男年十八以上者，人一頃，其八十畝為口分，二十畝為永業；

translations.literal: Under the land-grant system, each ding and each male eighteen or older received one qing; of this eighty mu were koufen and twenty mu were yongye;
translations.idiomatic: Each adult male and each man of eighteen or over received one qing of land: eighty mu as per-capita allotment and twenty mu as hereditary holding;

sentences.zh: 老及篤疾、廢疾者，人四十畝，寡妻妾三十畝，當戶者增二十畝，皆以二十畝為永業，其余為口分。

translations.literal: the elderly and those with severe or crippling illness received forty mu each; widows and concubines thirty mu; household heads received an additional twenty mu; in each case twenty mu were yongye and the rest koufen.
translations.idiomatic: the aged and the seriously disabled received forty mu each; widows and concubines thirty; heads of household gained another twenty. In every case twenty mu were hereditary and the remainder per-capita allotments.

sentences.zh: 永業之田，樹以榆、棗、桑及所宜之木，皆有數。

translations.literal: On yongye fields they planted elms, jujubes, mulberries, and trees suited to the soil, each in fixed numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary plots had to be planted with prescribed numbers of elms, jujubes, mulberries, and other suitable trees.

sentences.zh: 田多可以足其人者為寬鄉，少者為狹鄉。

translations.literal: Where land was abundant enough to satisfy the people it was called a broad district; where scarce, a narrow district.
translations.idiomatic: Districts with enough land for everyone were "broad"; those without were "narrow."

sentences.zh: 狹鄉授田，減寬鄉之半。

translations.literal: In narrow districts grants were reduced by half compared with broad districts.
translations.idiomatic: Narrow districts received half the allotment of broad ones.

sentences.zh: 其地有薄厚，歲一易者，倍受之。

translations.literal: Where soil was thin or fields were rotated yearly, grants were doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Poor soil or land rotated every year received double allotments.

sentences.zh: 寬鄉三易者，不倍授。

translations.literal: In broad districts with three-year rotation, grants were not doubled.
translations.idiomatic: In broad districts with three-year rotation, no doubling applied.

sentences.zh: 工商者，寬鄉減半，狹鄉不給。

translations.literal: Merchants and artisans in broad districts received half; in narrow districts they received none.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants and artisans in broad districts got half allotments; in narrow districts they received none.

sentences.zh: 凡庶人徙鄉及貧無以葬者，得賣世業田。

translations.literal: Commoners who moved districts or were too poor to bury their dead might sell their shiye fields.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners relocating or too poor for funerals might sell their hereditary plots.

sentences.zh: 自狹鄉而徙寬鄉者，得並賣口分田。

translations.literal: Those moving from a narrow to a broad district might also sell their koufen fields.
translations.idiomatic: Those moving from narrow to broad districts could sell their per-capita allotments as well.

sentences.zh: 已賣者，不復授。

translations.literal: Once sold, fields were not granted again.
translations.idiomatic: Land sold was never re-allotted.

sentences.zh: 死者收之，以授無田者。

translations.literal: At death the fields were reclaimed and granted to the landless.
translations.idiomatic: On death the state reclaimed the land and gave it to those without fields.

sentences.zh: 凡收授皆以歲十月。

translations.literal: All reclamation and granting took place in the tenth month of the year.
translations.idiomatic: Reclamation and new grants were carried out every year in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 授田先貧及有課役者。

translations.literal: Grants went first to the poor and those with tax obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Land was allotted first to the poor and to households liable for tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 凡田，鄉有余以給比鄉，縣有余以給比縣，州有余以給近州。

translations.literal: In general, surplus land in a district supplied neighboring districts; surplus in a county supplied neighboring counties; surplus in a prefecture supplied nearby prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus land in a district went to neighboring districts, county surpluses to neighboring counties, and prefectural surpluses to nearby prefectures.

sentences.zh: 凡授田者，丁歲輸粟二斛，稻三斛，謂之租。

translations.literal: All who received fields paid each ding year two hu of grain or three hu of rice—this was called zu.
translations.idiomatic: Every grantee paid two hu of grain or three of rice per adult male per year—the grain tax called zu.

sentences.zh: 丁隨鄉所出，歲輸絹二匹，綾、絁二丈，布加五之一，綿三兩，麻三斤，非蠶鄉則輸銀十四兩，謂之調。

translations.literal: Each ding paid according to local products: yearly two bolts of silk, two zhang of ling and shi, cloth with one-fifth added, three liang of cotton, three jin of hemp; in non-sericulture districts, fourteen liang of silver—this was called diao.
translations.idiomatic: Each adult male paid local produce: two bolts of silk, two zhang of fine cloth, extra cloth by one-fifth, three liang of cotton floss, three jin of hemp—or fourteen liang of silver where sericulture did not exist. This was the diao levy.

sentences.zh: 用人之力，歲二十日，閏加二日，不役者日為絹三尺，謂之庸。

translations.literal: Labor was levied twenty days a year, with two added in intercalary years; those not serving paid three chi of silk per day—this was called yong.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée labor ran twenty days a year, plus two in leap years; those who bought out of service paid three chi of silk per day—the yong levy.

sentences.zh: 有事而加役二十五日者免調，三十日者租、調皆免。

translations.literal: When special service added twenty-five days, diao was waived; at thirty days, both zu and diao were waived.
translations.idiomatic: Extra corvée of twenty-five days exempted diao; at thirty days both zu and diao were waived.

sentences.zh: 通正役不過五十日。

translations.literal: Regular corvée in total did not exceed fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: Regular corvée in all could not exceed fifty days.

sentences.zh: 自王公以下，皆有永業田。

translations.literal: From princes and dukes downward, all held yongye fields.
translations.idiomatic: From princes and dukes down, every rank held hereditary land.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后、皇太后、皇后緦麻以上親，內命婦一品以上親，郡王及五品以上祖父兄弟，職事、勛官三品以上有封者若縣男父子，國子、太學、四門學生、俊士，孝子、順孫、義夫、節婦同籍者，皆免課役。

translations.literal: Relatives of the grand empress dowager, empress dowager, and empress within sima mourning; relatives of inner consorts of first rank and above; grandfathers and brothers of princes and fifth-rank officials and above; officeholders and merit officials of third rank and above with fiefs, or county marquises and their sons; students of the Directorate, Imperial University, Four Gates, and jinshi candidates; filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives registered together—all were exempt from tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Kin of the empresses within the five degrees of mourning, kin of high-ranking inner consorts, kin of princes and fifth-rank officials, third-rank officials and merit nobles with fiefs and their sons, imperial students and candidates, and registered filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives were all exempt from tax and labor.

sentences.zh: 凡主戶內有課口者為課戶。

translations.literal: Households with taxable members within the chief household were called tax households.
translations.idiomatic: A chief household with liable members was a tax household.

sentences.zh: 若老及男廢疾、篤疾、寡妻妾、部曲、客女、奴婢及視九品以上官，不課。

translations.literal: The elderly, males with crippling or severe illness, widows and concubines, retainers, tenant women, slaves, and those treated as ninth-rank officials and above were not taxed.
translations.idiomatic: The aged, disabled men, the seriously ill, widows and concubines, retainers, tenant women, slaves, and households ranked as ninth-grade officials or higher paid no tax.

sentences.zh: 凡裏有手實，歲終具民之年與地之闊狹，為鄉帳。

translations.literal: Each li kept a household register; at year's end it listed people's ages and the breadth of their land, forming the district account.
translations.idiomatic: Each neighborhood kept household registers; at year-end ages and land holdings were compiled into the district roll.

sentences.zh: 鄉成於縣，縣成於州，州成於戶部。

translations.literal: District accounts were consolidated at the county, county at the prefecture, prefecture at the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: District rolls went to the county, county rolls to the prefecture, prefectural rolls to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 又有計帳，具來歲課役以報度支。

translations.literal: There was also a projected account listing the next year's taxes and corvée to report to the Department of Public Works and Finance.
translations.idiomatic: A projected account also listed the coming year's taxes and corvée for the treasury.

sentences.zh: 國有所須，先奏而斂。

translations.literal: When the state had needs, it memorialized first and then levied.
translations.idiomatic: State levies required prior memorial and approval.

sentences.zh: 凡稅斂之數，書於縣門、村坊，與眾知之。

translations.literal: All tax figures were posted at county gates and village wards so the public would know.
translations.idiomatic: Tax schedules were posted at county gates and village wards for all to see.

sentences.zh: 水、旱、霜、蝗耗十四者，免其租；

translations.literal: Flood, drought, frost, and locust damage of four-tenths exempted zu;
translations.idiomatic: Flood, drought, frost, or locust loss of four-tenths exempted the grain tax;

sentences.zh: 桑麻盡者，免其調；

translations.literal: total loss of mulberry and hemp exempted diao;
translations.idiomatic: total loss of mulberry and hemp exempted the diao levy;

sentences.zh: 田耗十之六者，免租調；

translations.literal: field loss of six-tenths exempted zu and diao;
translations.idiomatic: field loss of six-tenths exempted both zu and diao;

sentences.zh: 耗七者，課、役皆免。

translations.literal: loss of seven-tenths exempted all taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: loss of seven-tenths exempted all taxes and labor service.

sentences.zh: 凡新附之戶，春以三月免役，夏以六月免課，秋以九月課、役皆免。

translations.literal: Newly registered households: in spring, corvée waived for three months; in summer, taxes waived for six months; in autumn, both taxes and corvée waived for nine months.
translations.idiomatic: New households joining in spring were exempt from corvée for three months; in summer from taxes for six months; in autumn from both for nine months.

sentences.zh: 徙寬鄉者，縣覆於州，出境則覆於戶部，官以閑月達之。

translations.literal: Those moving to broad districts were verified by the county to the prefecture; crossing borders, verified to the Ministry of Revenue; officials reported in slack months.
translations.idiomatic: Migrants to broad districts were certified county to prefecture, and across borders to the Ministry of Revenue; officials filed reports in the off-season.

sentences.zh: 自畿內徙畿外，自京縣徙余縣，皆有禁。

translations.literal: Moving from the inner to the outer capital districts, or from capital counties to other counties, was all restricted.
translations.idiomatic: Moves from the capital core to the outer districts, or from metropolitan counties to ordinary counties, were restricted.

sentences.zh: 四夷降戶，附以寬鄉，給復十年。

translations.literal: Surrendered households of the four barbarians were settled in broad districts with ten years' exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered frontier peoples were settled in broad districts with ten years' tax relief.

sentences.zh: 奴婢縱為良人，給復三年。

translations.literal: Slaves manumitted to commoner status received three years' exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Freed slaves received three years' exemption.

sentences.zh: 沒外蕃人，一年還者給復三年，二年者給復四年，三年者給復五年。

translations.literal: Frontier men captured abroad: those returning within one year received three years' exemption; within two years, four years'; within three years, five years'.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier men captured abroad who returned within one year got three years' relief; within two years, four; within three, five.

sentences.zh: 浮民、部曲、客女、奴婢縱為良者附寬鄉。

translations.literal: Floating population, retainers, tenant women, and slaves manumitted to commoners were attached to broad districts.
translations.idiomatic: Vagrants, retainers, tenant women, and freed slaves were registered in broad districts.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，初稅草以給諸閑，而驛馬有牧田。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, a grass tax was first levied to supply various incidentals, and relay horses had pasture fields.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan a fodder tax was introduced for miscellaneous expenses, and post horses were given pasture land.

sentences.zh: 太宗方銳意於治，官吏考課，以鰥寡少者進考，如增戶法；

translations.literal: Taizong was then intent on good government; in officials' performance reviews, few widowers and orphans advanced one's rating, as with the household-increase law;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was bent on good government; in performance reviews, few widows and orphans in a district improved an official's rating, as with the household-growth rule;

sentences.zh: 失勸導者以減戶論。

translations.literal: failure to encourage settlement was judged as household decrease.
translations.idiomatic: failure to encourage settlement counted as a loss of households.

sentences.zh: 配租以斂穫早晚、險易、遠近為差。

translations.literal: Zu collection was scheduled by harvest timing, terrain difficulty, and distance.
translations.idiomatic: Grain tax deadlines varied with harvest season, terrain, and distance.

sentences.zh: 庸、調輸以八月，發以九月。

translations.literal: Yong and diao were delivered in the eighth month and dispatched in the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and diao were collected in the eighth month and forwarded in the ninth.

sentences.zh: 同時輸者先遠民。

translations.literal: When delivery times coincided, distant subjects went first.
translations.idiomatic: When deadlines overlapped, distant districts paid first.

sentences.zh: 皆自概量。

translations.literal: All measured their own dues.
translations.idiomatic: Households measured their own deliveries.

sentences.zh: 州府歲市土所出為貢，其價視絹之上下，無過五十匹。

translations.literal: Prefectures yearly purchased local products as tribute; value was set by silk grades, not exceeding fifty bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Each year prefectures bought local products as tribute, priced by silk grade, capped at fifty bolts.

sentences.zh: 異物、滋味、口馬、鷹犬，非有詔不獻。

translations.literal: Exotic goods, delicacies, horses for the mouth, hawks and dogs—without an edict they were not presented.
translations.idiomatic: Exotic goods, delicacies, riding horses, hawks, and hunting dogs were not sent without imperial order.

sentences.zh: 有加配，則以代租賦。

translations.literal: When extra assignments were made, they substituted for zu and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Extra tribute assignments could substitute for regular taxes.

sentences.zh: 其兇荒則有社倉賑給，不足則徙民就食諸州。

translations.literal: In famine there were community granaries for relief; if insufficient, people were moved to eat in other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In famine community granaries provided relief; if stores ran short, people were relocated to other prefectures for food.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞戴胄建議：「自王公以下，計墾田，秋熟，所在為義倉，歲兇以給民。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Dai Zhou proposed: "From princes and dukes downward, reckon cultivated fields; after the autumn harvest, establish charity granaries everywhere to supply the people in famine years."
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Dai Zhou proposed: "From princes down, tally cultivated land; after harvest, set up charity granaries in each locality to feed the people in bad years."

sentences.zh: 」太宗善之，乃詔：「畝稅二升，粟、麥、秔、稻，隨土地所宜。

translations.literal: Taizong approved and issued an edict: "Two sheng per mu in tax, millet, wheat, husked rice, or paddy as the land suits."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong approved and ordered: "Two sheng per mu, in millet, wheat, husked rice, or paddy as local conditions allow."

sentences.zh: 寬鄉斂以所種，狹鄉據青苗簿而督之。

translations.literal: Broad districts collected according to what was planted; narrow districts enforced collection by the green-crop register.
translations.idiomatic: Broad districts levied on actual crops; narrow districts used the green-crop register to enforce collection.

sentences.zh: 田耗十四者免其半，耗十七者皆免之。

translations.literal: Field loss of four-tenths halved the levy; loss of seven-tenths exempted it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Crop loss of four-tenths halved the levy; loss of seven-tenths canceled it.

sentences.zh: 商賈無田者，以其戶為九等，出粟自五石至於五斗為差。

translations.literal: Merchants without land were ranked in nine household grades, paying grain from five shi down to five dou by grade.
translations.idiomatic: Landless merchants were ranked in nine grades and paid grain from five shi down to five dou.

sentences.zh: 下下戶及夷獠不取焉。

translations.literal: The lowest grade and tribal peoples were not levied.
translations.idiomatic: The poorest households and tribal peoples were exempt.

sentences.zh: 歲不登，則以賑民；

translations.literal: In lean years it was used to relieve the people;
translations.idiomatic: In bad years the grain relieved the people;

sentences.zh: 或貸為種子，則至秋而償。

translations.literal: or lent as seed grain, to be repaid by autumn.
translations.idiomatic: or lent as seed to be repaid at harvest.

sentences.zh: 」其後洛、相、幽、徐、齊、並、秦、蒲州又置常平倉，粟藏九年，米藏五年，下濕之地，粟藏五年，米藏三年，皆著於令。

translations.literal: Later Luoyang, Xiang, You, Xu, Qi, Bing, Qin, and Pu prefectures also established ever-normal granaries: grain stored nine years, rice five; in damp lowlands, grain five years and rice three—all written into statute.
translations.idiomatic: Later ever-normal granaries were added at Luoyang, Xiang, You, Xu, Qi, Bing, Qin, and Pu: grain stored nine years, rice five—in damp regions, grain five and rice three—all codified in law.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，戶不及三百萬，絹一匹易米一斗。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan, households numbered less than three million; one bolt of silk bought one dou of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan there were fewer than three million households, and one bolt of silk bought only one dou of rice.

sentences.zh: 至四年，米斗四五錢，外戶不閉者數月，馬牛被野，人行數千里不賫糧，民物蕃息，四夷降附者百二十萬人。

translations.literal: By the fourth year, rice was four or five cash per dou; outer gates went unbarred for months; horses and cattle roamed the wilds; travelers went thousands of li without carrying grain; people and goods flourished; a million two hundred thousand of the four barbarians submitted.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year rice cost four or five cash per dou; outer gates stood open for months; horses and cattle grazed freely; travelers went thousands of li without provisions; population and wealth grew; and 1.2 million frontier peoples submitted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下斷獄，死罪者二十九人，號稱太平。

translations.literal: That year, capital cases throughout the realm numbered twenty-nine death sentences; it was called the Great Peace.
translations.idiomatic: That year only twenty-nine death sentences were handed down empire-wide—the age was called Great Peace.

sentences.zh: 此高祖、太宗致治之大略，及其成效如此。

translations.literal: This was the great outline by which Gaozu and Taizong brought order, and such were its results.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the broad policy by which Gaozu and Taizong brought order—and such were its results.

sentences.zh: 高宗承之，海內艾安。

translations.literal: Gaozong inherited it, and within the seas all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong inherited this legacy, and the realm knew peace.

sentences.zh: 太尉長孫無忌等輔政，天下未見失德。

translations.literal: Grand Mentor Zhangsun Wuji and others assisted in government; the realm saw no loss of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhangsun Wuji and others guiding policy, the court showed no grave misconduct.

sentences.zh: 數引刺史入閤，問民疾苦。

translations.literal: He repeatedly summoned prefectural governors into the palace to ask about the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He often summoned prefects to court to inquire after the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 即位之歲，增戶十五萬。

translations.literal: In the year of his accession, households increased by one hundred fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In his first year on the throne, registered households rose by 150,000.

sentences.zh: 及中書令李義府、侍中許敬宗既用事，役費並起。

translations.literal: When Chief Minister Li Yifu and Attendant-in-Ordinary Xu Jingzong came to power, corvée and expenditures rose together.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Yifu and Xu Jingzong held power, corvée and spending both surged.

sentences.zh: 永淳以後，給用益不足。

translations.literal: After Yongchun, supplies grew ever more insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongchun era, revenue fell ever shorter of need.

sentences.zh: 加以武後之亂，紀綱大壞，民不勝其毒。

translations.literal: Added to this was the turmoil of Empress Wu; institutions were greatly ruined, and the people could not bear the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Then came Empress Wu's turmoil: law and order collapsed, and the people could not endure the burden.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初立求治，蠲徭役者給蠲符，以流外及九品京官為蠲使，歲再遣之。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong first took the throne seeking good government, those exempted from corvée received exemption tallies; officials outside the regular roster and capital officials of the ninth rank served as exemption commissioners, dispatched twice yearly.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong first sought reform, corvée exemptions were issued on tallies; minor officials and ninth-rank capital appointees served as exemption commissioners, sent out twice a year.

sentences.zh: 開元八年，頒庸調法於天下，好不過精，惡不至濫，闊者一尺八寸，長者四丈。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan, the yong and diao law was promulgated empire-wide: the finest not beyond refined quality, the poorest not below acceptable grade; width at least one chi eight cun, length at most four zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 8 the yong-diao standards were issued empire-wide: finest cloth not above refined grade, poorest not below acceptable; width at least 1.8 chi, length at most 4 zhang.

sentences.zh: 然是時天下戶未嘗升降。

translations.literal: Yet at this time household registers throughout the realm had never been revised up or down.
translations.idiomatic: Yet household registers had never been properly updated.

sentences.zh: 監察御史宇文融獻策：括籍外羨田、逃戶，自占者給復五年，每丁稅錢千五百，以攝御史分行括實。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Yuwen Rong proposed a plan: register surplus fields and absconding households outside the rolls; self-reporting received five years' exemption; each ding paid 1,500 cash in tax; acting censors were sent in branches to verify and register.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yuwen Rong proposed surveying hidden land and unregistered households: voluntary registration won five years' relief; each adult male paid 1,500 cash; acting censors fanned out to verify the rolls.

sentences.zh: 陽翟尉皇甫憬上書言其不可。

translations.literal: Assistant Magistrate of Yangdi Huangfu Jing memorialized that it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yangdi Assistant Magistrate Huangfu Jing memorialized against the plan.

sentences.zh: 玄宗方任用融，乃貶憬為盈川尉。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was then employing Rong and demoted Jing to Assistant Magistrate of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong, backing Rong, demoted Jing to magistrate of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 諸道所括得客戶八十余萬，田亦稱是。

translations.literal: The various circuits registered more than eight hundred thousand client households, and fields in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: The circuits registered over 800,000 client households, with land to match.

sentences.zh: 州縣希旨張虛數，以正田為羨，編戶為客，歲終，籍錢數百萬緡。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties, eager to please, inflated false figures, treating regular fields as surplus and registered households as clients; by year's end they registered several million strings in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials eager to please inflated the rolls, reclassified regular land as surplus and registered households as clients, and by year-end reported several million strings in revenue.

sentences.zh: 十六年，乃詔每三歲以九等定籍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict ordered household registers fixed by nine grades every three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, the court ordered household registers revised by nine grades every three years.

sentences.zh: 而庸調折租所取華好，州縣長宮勸織，中書門下察濫惡以貶官吏，精者褒賞之。

translations.literal: Yong and diao and grain-tax substitutes were required in fine quality; prefectural and county chiefs urged weaving; the Secretariat inspected shoddy goods to demote officials and rewarded the finest.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, diao, and grain substitutes had to be of fine quality; local chiefs urged weaving; the Secretariat punished officials for shoddy goods and rewarded excellence.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，詔男十五、女十三以上得嫁娶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, an edict allowed males fifteen and females thirteen and above to marry.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 22, males of fifteen and females of thirteen were permitted to marry.

sentences.zh: 州縣歲上戶口登耗，采訪使覆實之，刺史、縣令以為課最。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties yearly reported household increases and decreases; investigating commissioners verified them; governors and magistrates were judged by this in performance reviews.
translations.idiomatic: Each year counties reported household growth; investigating commissioners verified the figures; governors and magistrates were rated on the results.

sentences.zh: 初，永徽中禁買賣世業、口分田。

translations.literal: Initially, in the Yonghui era, sale of shiye and koufen fields was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yonghui era, sale of hereditary and per-capita fields was banned.

sentences.zh: 其後豪富兼並，貧者失業，於是詔買者還地而罰之。

translations.literal: Later the wealthy consolidated holdings and the poor lost their livelihoods; an edict then ordered buyers to return the land and punished them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the rich absorbed land and the poor lost their farms; buyers were ordered to return land and were punished.

sentences.zh: 先是楊州租、調以錢，嶺南以米，安南以絲，益州以羅、䌷、綾、絹供春彩。

translations.literal: Previously Yangzhou paid zu and diao in cash, Lingnan in rice, Annan in silk, and Yizhou supplied gauze, silk, ling, and juan for spring tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou had paid zu and diao in cash, Lingnan in rice, Annan in silk, and Yizhou furnished gauze and silks for spring tribute.

sentences.zh: 因詔江南亦以布代租。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered the Jiangnan region also to pay zu in cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Jiangnan to pay the grain tax in cloth as well.

sentences.zh: 中書令李林甫以租庸、丁防、和糴、春彩、稅草無定法，歲為旨符，遣使一告，費紙五十余萬。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Linfu, because zu-yong, frontier garrisons, government grain purchases, spring tribute, and fodder tax had no fixed law and yearly edict slips were sent by messenger at once, costing more than five hundred thousand sheets of paper.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Linfu noted that zu-yong, frontier service, grain purchases, spring tribute, and fodder tax lacked fixed rules; yearly edict slips sent by messenger consumed over half a million sheets of paper.

sentences.zh: 條目既多，覆問逾年，乃與采訪朝集使議革之，為長行旨，以授朝集使及送旨符使，歲有所支，進畫附驛以達，每州不過二紙。

translations.literal: Entries were so numerous that replies took more than a year; he then discussed reform with investigating and assembly commissioners, making standing edict guidelines for them and edict-bearers; yearly expenditures were listed, submitted by draft and relay, no more than two sheets per prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With so many items, replies took over a year; he reformed the system with investigating commissioners into standing guidelines, sent by relay—no more than two sheets per prefecture.

sentences.zh: 凡庸、調、租、資課，皆任土所宜，州縣長官涖定粗良，具上中下三物之樣輸京都。

translations.literal: All yong, diao, zu, and resource levies followed local products; prefectural and county chiefs set coarse and fine grades and sent samples of upper, middle, and lower goods to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, diao, zu, and resource levies followed local products; local chiefs set quality grades and sent upper, middle, and lower samples to the capital.

sentences.zh: 有濫惡，督中物之直。

translations.literal: If goods were shoddy, the middle grade's price was enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Shoddy goods were priced at the middle grade.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以江、淮輸運有河、洛之艱，而關中蠶桑少，菽粟常賤，乃命庸、調、資課皆以米，兇年樂輸布絹者亦從之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, because Jiang-Huai transport faced difficulties at the Yellow and Luo rivers, while Guanzhong had little sericulture and beans and grain were cheap, yong, diao, and resource levies were ordered paid in rice; in famine years those willing to pay in cloth and silk were also allowed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 25, because Jiang-Huai grain faced transport bottlenecks at the Yellow and Luo while Guanzhong lacked silk and grain was cheap, yong, diao, and resource levies were paid in rice; in famine years cloth and silk were accepted.

sentences.zh: 河南、北不通運州，租皆為絹，代關中庸、課，詔度支減轉運。

translations.literal: In Henan north and south, where transport prefectures were unreachable, zu was all paid in silk to substitute for Guanzhong yong and levies; the Department of Public Works was ordered to reduce transport.
translations.idiomatic: In north and south Henan, unreachable by transport routes, grain tax was paid in silk to supply Guanzhong corvée and levies, and transport was reduced.

sentences.zh: 明年，又詔民三歲以下為黃，十五以下為小，二十以下為中。

translations.literal: The next year, an edict made those under three huang, under fifteen xiao, and under twenty zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, children under three were infants, under fifteen minors, and under twenty youths.

sentences.zh: 又以民間戶高丁多者，率與父母別籍異居，以避征戍，乃詔十丁以上免二丁，五丁以上免一丁，侍丁孝者免徭役。

translations.literal: Because wealthy households with many adult males commonly split registers and lived apart from parents to avoid conscription, an edict exempted two ding from households of ten or more and one from five or more; filial attendants were exempt from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households with many sons often split registers to evade conscription; households of ten ding lost two, of five lost one, and filial attendants were exempt from corvée.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載，更民十八以上為中男，二十三以上成丁。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, males eighteen and above became zhongnan; twenty-three and above became ding.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 3, males of eighteen became youths and those of twenty-three became adult males liable for tax.

sentences.zh: 五載，詔貧不能自濟者，每鄉免三十丁租庸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict exempted thirty ding per district from zu-yong for those too poor to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 5, each district exempted thirty ding from zu-yong for households too poor to survive.

sentences.zh: 男子七十五以上、婦人七十以上，中男一人為侍；

translations.literal: For men seventy-five and above and women seventy and above, one zhongnan served as attendant;
translations.idiomatic: For men seventy-five and women seventy, one youth was assigned as attendant;

sentences.zh: 八十以上以令式從事。

translations.literal: those eighty and above were treated according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: those eighty and above were governed by special statute.

sentences.zh: 是時，海內富實，米鬥之價錢十三，青、齊間鬥才三錢，絹一匹錢二百。

translations.literal: At this time the realm was rich and solid: rice thirteen cash per dou; in Qing and Qi only three cash; one bolt of silk two hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was prosperous: rice cost thirteen cash per dou, only three in Qing and Qi, and two hundred cash per bolt of silk.

sentences.zh: 道路列肆，具酒食以待行人，店有驛驢，行千里不持尺兵。

translations.literal: Shops lined the roads with food and drink for travelers; inns had relay donkeys; one traveled a thousand li without carrying a weapon.
translations.idiomatic: Roadside shops offered food and drink; inns kept relay donkeys; travelers went a thousand li unarmed.

sentences.zh: 天下歲入之物，租錢二百余萬緡，粟千九百八十余萬斛，庸、調絹七百四十萬匹，綿百八十余萬屯，布千三十五萬余端。

translations.literal: Annual revenue empire-wide: zu cash over two million strings, grain over nineteen million eight hundred thousand hu, yong and diao silk over seven million four hundred thousand bolts, cotton over one million eight hundred thousand tun, cloth over ten million thirty-five thousand duan.
translations.idiomatic: Annual revenue: over two million strings in grain tax cash, nearly twenty million hu of grain, 7.4 million bolts of yong-diao silk, 1.8 million tun of cotton, and over ten million duan of cloth.

sentences.zh: 天子驕於佚樂而用不知節，大抵用物之數，常過其所入。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven grew proud in ease and pleasure and did not restrain spending; generally what was used exceeded what came in.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor indulged in luxury and spent without restraint; expenditures routinely exceeded revenue.

sentences.zh: 於是錢谷之臣，始事朘刻。

translations.literal: Then ministers of revenue began to practice exaction.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue officials then turned to squeezing the people.

sentences.zh: 太府卿楊崇禮句剝分銖，有欠折漬損者，州縣督送，歷年不止。

translations.literal: Grand Treasury Director Yang Chongli parsed and stripped every fen and zhu; for shortages, spoilage, or damage, prefectures and counties were pressed to deliver, year after year without end.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Treasury Director Yang Chongli wrung out every penny; counties were hounded year after year for shortages and spoilage.

sentences.zh: 其子慎矜專知太府，次子慎名知京倉，亦以苛刻結主恩。

translations.literal: His son Shenjin managed the Grand Treasury; his second son Shenming managed the capital granaries; both also won favor through harshness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shenjin ran the Grand Treasury and Shenming the capital granaries; both curried favor through harsh exaction.

sentences.zh: 王鉷為戶口色役使，歲進錢百億萬緡，非租庸正額者，積百寶大盈庫，以供天子燕私。

translations.literal: Wang Hong as Commissioner for Households and Miscellaneous Levies yearly presented ten billion strings; sums outside regular zu-yong quotas were stored in the Hundred Treasures Great Abundance Vault for the Son of Heaven's private pleasures.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong as household levy commissioner presented ten billion strings yearly; extralegal revenue filled the Great Abundance Vault for the emperor's private use.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山反，司空楊國忠以為正庫物不可以給士，遣侍御史崔眾至太原納錢度僧尼道士，旬日得百萬緡而已。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Minister of Works Yang Guozhong held that regular vault goods could not pay the troops; he sent Attending Censor Cui Zhong to Taiyuan to collect cash by ordaining monks and Daoist priests, gaining only a million strings in ten days.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Yang Guozhong, finding the regular treasury inadequate for troops, sent Censor Cui Zhong to Taiyuan to sell ordinations—and raised only a million strings in ten days.

sentences.zh: 自兩京陷沒，民物耗弊，天下蕭然。

translations.literal: From the fall of the two capitals, people and goods were exhausted; the realm was desolate.
translations.idiomatic: After both capitals fell, people and wealth were ruined and the empire lay in ruin.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，遣御史鄭叔清等籍江淮、蜀漢富商右族訾畜，十收其二，謂之率貸。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, he sent Censor Zheng Shuqing and others to register the wealth of great merchants and eminent families in Jiang-Huai, Shu, and Han, taking two-tenths of their assets—called "assessed lending."
translations.idiomatic: Suzong sent Zheng Shuqing to register wealthy families in Jiang-Huai and the southwest and seize two-tenths of their assets—the "assessed lending" levy.

sentences.zh: 諸道亦稅商賈以贍軍，錢一千者有稅。

translations.literal: The various circuits also taxed merchants to support the army; every thousand cash was taxed.
translations.idiomatic: Circuits taxed merchants to feed the armies—a tax on every thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 於是北海郡錄事參軍第五琦以錢谷得見，請於江淮置租庸使，吳鹽、蜀麻、銅冶皆有稅，市輕貨繇江陵、襄陽、上津路轉至鳳翔。

translations.literal: Then Diwu Qi of Beihai, a recording secretary, gained audience through fiscal expertise and requested zu-yong commissioners in Jiang-Huai; Wu salt, Shu hemp, and copper smelting were all taxed; light goods were purchased and routed via Jiangling, Xiangyang, and Shangjin to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Diwu Qi of Beihai, a clerk who impressed the court with fiscal expertise, proposed zu-yong commissioners in Jiang-Huai; salt, hemp, and copper were taxed; light goods were routed through Jiangling and Xiangyang to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 明年，鄭叔清與宰相裴冕建議，以天下用度不充，諸道得召人納錢，給空名告身，授官勛邑號；

translations.literal: The next year, Zheng Shuqing and Chief Minister Pei Mian proposed that because empire-wide expenditures were insufficient, circuits might summon men to pay cash for blank appointment documents, granting offices, merit titles, and fief names;
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zheng Shuqing and Pei Mian proposed that circuits sell blank appointments for cash—offices, merit titles, and fief names;

sentences.zh: 度道士僧尼不可勝計；

translations.literal: ordained Daoist priests, monks, and nuns beyond counting;
translations.idiomatic: ordained countless monks and priests;

sentences.zh: 納錢百千，賜明經出身；

translations.literal: those paying a hundred or a thousand strings received mingjing degrees;
translations.idiomatic: a hundred or a thousand strings bought a classics degree;

sentences.zh: 商賈助軍者，給復。

translations.literal: merchants aiding the army received tax exemption.
translations.idiomatic: merchants who aided the army received tax relief.

sentences.zh: 及兩京平，又於關輔諸州，納錢度道士僧尼萬人。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered, ten thousand monks and priests were ordained for cash in the Guanfu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After the capitals were recovered, ten thousand ordinations were sold for cash in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 而百姓殘於兵盜，米鬥至錢七千，鬻籺為糧，民行乞食者屬路。

translations.literal: Yet the people were ravaged by war and bandits; rice reached seven thousand cash per dou; chaff was sold as grain; beggars lined the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The people were ravaged by war; rice cost seven thousand cash per dou; chaff was sold as food; beggars filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 乃詔能賑貧乏者，寵以爵衤失。

translations.literal: An edict then honored those who could relieve the poor with noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded those who relieved the poor with titles of honor.

sentences.zh: 故事，天下財賦歸左藏，而太府以時上其數，尚書比部覆其出入。

translations.literal: By precedent, empire-wide revenue went to the Left Vault; the Grand Treasury reported figures in season; the Ministry of Revenue's comparison section audited receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, revenue went to the Left Vault; the Grand Treasury reported totals; the Ministry audited all receipts and spending.

sentences.zh: 是時，京師豪將假取不能禁，第五琦為度支鹽鐵使，請皆歸大盈庫，供天子給賜，主以中官。

translations.literal: At this time capital generals borrowed from the vault without restraint; Diwu Qi as Salt and Iron Commissioner requested all funds go to the Great Abundance Vault for the Son of Heaven's gifts, managed by eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Capital generals looted the treasury at will; Diwu Qi as salt commissioner moved all funds to the Great Abundance Vault for imperial gifts, managed by eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 自是天下之財為人君私藏，有司不得程其多少。

translations.literal: From then on the realm's wealth became the ruler's private store; officials could not measure how much.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth imperial wealth became the emperor's private hoard, beyond official accounting.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，詔一戶三丁者免一丁，凡畝稅二升，男子二十五為成丁，五十五為老，以優民。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde, an edict exempted one ding from households of three; grain tax was two sheng per mu; males became ding at twenty-five and lao at fifty-five, to ease the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde 1, households of three ding lost one; grain tax was two sheng per mu; adult liability began at twenty-five and ended at fifty-five—to ease the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 而強寇未夷，民耗斂重。

translations.literal: Yet powerful bandits were not pacified; the people were exhausted and levies heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rebels remained unpacified; the people were exhausted and taxes crushing.

sentences.zh: 及吐蕃逼京師，近甸屯兵數萬，百官進俸錢，又率戶以給軍糧。

translations.literal: When Tibetans pressed the capital, tens of thousands camped in nearby districts; officials contributed salary funds; households were levied again for army grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans threatened the capital, tens of thousands of troops encamped nearby; officials donated salaries and households were levied again for army grain.

sentences.zh: 至大歷元年，詔流民還者，給復二年，田園盡，則授以逃田。

translations.literal: By the first year of Dali, returning refugees received two years' exemption; if their fields were gone, abandoned land was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 1, returning refugees got two years' relief; if their land was lost, they received abandoned fields.

sentences.zh: 天下苗一畝稅錢十五，市輕貨給百官手力課。

translations.literal: Empire-wide, fifteen cash per mu in seedling tax; light goods were purchased to pay officials' labor levies.
translations.idiomatic: A seedling tax of fifteen cash per mu was levied empire-wide; light goods were bought to pay officials' service fees.

sentences.zh: 以國用急，不及秋，方苗青即征之，號「青苗錢」又有「地頭錢」，每畝二十，通名為青苗錢。

translations.literal: Because state needs were urgent, before autumn when seedlings were still green they were levied—called "green-crop money"; there was also "field-head money" of twenty per mu; both were commonly called green-crop money.
translations.idiomatic: With the treasury desperate, tax was collected while seedlings were still green—the "green-crop levy"; plus a "field-head" fee of twenty per mu; both were called green-crop money.

sentences.zh: 又詔上都秋稅分二等，上等畝稅一斗，下等六升，荒田畝稅二升。

translations.literal: An edict also set upper capital autumn tax in two grades: upper fields one dou per mu, lower six sheng, wasteland two sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's autumn tax was split: upper fields one dou per mu, lower six sheng, wasteland two sheng.

sentences.zh: 五年，始定法：夏，上田畝稅六升，下田畝四升；

translations.literal: In the fifth year, law was fixed: in summer, upper fields six sheng per mu, lower four sheng;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year rates were fixed: summer tax—upper fields six sheng per mu, lower four;

sentences.zh: 秋，上田畝稅五升，下田畝三升；

translations.literal: in autumn, upper fields five sheng per mu, lower three sheng;
translations.idiomatic: autumn tax—upper fields five sheng, lower three;

sentences.zh: 荒田如故；

translations.literal: wasteland as before;
translations.idiomatic: wasteland unchanged;

sentences.zh: 青苗錢畝加一倍，而地頭錢不在焉。

translations.literal: green-crop money was doubled per mu, but field-head money was not included.
translations.idiomatic: the green-crop levy was doubled per mu, excluding the field-head fee.

sentences.zh: 初，轉運使掌外，度支使掌內。

translations.literal: Initially, transport commissioners managed external revenue and expenditure commissioners managed internal.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioners managed external revenue; expenditure commissioners managed internal funds.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年，分天下財賦、鑄錢、常平、轉運、鹽鐵，置二使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongtai, empire-wide revenue, coinage, ever-normal granaries, transport, and salt and iron were divided between two commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 2, fiscal authority—revenue, minting, granaries, transport, and salt—was split between two commissioners.

sentences.zh: 東都畿內、河南、淮南、江東西、湖南、荊南、山南東道，以轉運使劉晏領之；

translations.literal: Eastern capital metropolitan area, Henan, Huainan, Jiangdong west, Hunan, Jingnan, and Shannan east circuit were led by Transport Commissioner Liu Yan;
translations.idiomatic: The eastern circuits—including the capital region, Henan, Huainan, and the lower Yangzi—fell to Transport Commissioner Liu Yan;

sentences.zh: 京畿、關內、河東、劍南、山南西道，以京兆尹、判度支第五琦領之。

translations.literal: Capital metropolitan area, Guannei, Hedong, Jiannan, and Shannan west circuit were led by Metropolitan Governor and Acting Expenditure Commissioner Diwu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The western circuits—the capital, Guanzhong, Hedong, and Sichuan—went to Metropolitan Governor Diwu Qi.

sentences.zh: 及琦貶，以戶部侍郎、判度支韓滉與晏分治。

translations.literal: When Qi was demoted, Vice Minister of Revenue and Acting Expenditure Commissioner Han Huang shared administration with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi's demotion, Han Huang as vice minister of revenue shared fiscal duties with Yan.

sentences.zh: 時回紇有助收西京功，代宗厚遇之，與中國婚姻，歲送馬十萬匹，酬以縑帛百余萬匹。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs had aided in recovering the western capital; Daizong treated them generously, marrying into the Chinese imperial house; yearly they sent one hundred thousand horses, repaid with over a million bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs had helped retake Chang'an; Daizong favored them with marriage alliances; they sent a hundred thousand horses yearly, paid for with over a million bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 而中國財力屈竭，歲負馬價。

translations.literal: Yet China's finances were exhausted, falling short on the horse price each year.
translations.idiomatic: China's treasury was exhausted, falling short on the horse payments every year.

sentences.zh: 河、湟六鎮既陷，歲發防秋兵三萬戍京西，資糧百五十余萬緡。

translations.literal: After the six He-Huang garrisons fell, thirty thousand autumn-defense troops were sent yearly to garrison western Jing, costing over 1.5 million strings in supplies.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hexi garrisons fell, thirty thousand autumn-defense troops garrisoned the west yearly at a cost of 1.5 million strings.

sentences.zh: 而中官魚朝恩方恃恩擅權，代宗與宰相元載日夜圖之。

translations.literal: Eunuch Yu Chao'en relied on favor and usurped power; Daizong and Chief Minister Yuan Zai plotted against him day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Yu Chao'en abused imperial favor; Daizong and Yuan Zai plotted against him day and night.

sentences.zh: 及朝恩誅，帝復與載貳，君臣猜間不協，邊計兵食，置而不議者幾十年。

translations.literal: After Chao'en was executed, the emperor again turned against Zai; ruler and minister were mutually suspicious; frontier plans for troops and grain went undiscussed for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: After Chao'en's death, emperor and minister turned on each other; frontier defense and supply went undiscussed for nearly a decade.

sentences.zh: 而諸鎮擅地，結為表裏，日治兵繕壘，天子不能繩以法，顓留意祠禱、焚幣玉、寫浮屠書，度支稟賜僧巫，歲以鉅萬計。

translations.literal: Regional commanders seized territory and allied inside and out, daily drilling troops and repairing walls; the Son of Heaven could not restrain them by law and devoted himself to sacrifices, burning jade and silk, copying Buddhist scriptures; the expenditure office granted alms to monks and shamans by tens of thousands yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Regional warlords seized territory, armed themselves, and defied the court; the emperor turned to sacrifices, burning jade offerings, and copying sutras—the treasury gave monks and shamans tens of thousands yearly.

sentences.zh: 然帝性儉約，身所禦衣，必浣染至再三，欲以先天下。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor was frugal by nature; garments he wore were washed and dyed two or three times, wishing to lead the realm by example.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor was personally frugal, wearing his robes until they were washed threadbare, hoping to set an example.

sentences.zh: 然生日、端午，四方貢獻至數千萬者，加以恩澤，而諸道尚侈麗以自媚。

translations.literal: Yet on his birthday and the Dragon Boat Festival, tribute from the four directions reached tens of millions; added to his largesse, circuits still favored extravagance to please him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet birthday and Dragon Boat Festival tributes ran to tens of millions; on top of imperial gifts, circuits competed in lavish display.

sentences.zh: 朝多留事，經歲不能遣，置客省以居，上封事不足采者、蕃夷貢獻未報及失職未敘者，食度支數千百人。

translations.literal: Court business piled up, undispatched for years; a Guest Bureau was established to house them—memorials not adopted, barbarian tribute unanswered, and officials dismissed but not reassigned—numbering thousands on the expenditure office's payroll.
translations.idiomatic: Court business backed up for years; a Guest Bureau housed rejected memorialists, unanswered envoys, and unreinstated officials—thousands on the treasury payroll.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，用宰相崔祐甫，拘客省者出之，食度支者遣之，歲省費萬計。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne, he employed Chief Minister Cui Youfu, released those detained in the Guest Bureau, dismissed those on the expenditure payroll, and saved tens of thousands yearly.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong succeeded, Cui Youfu released Guest Bureau detainees and cut treasury deadwood, saving tens of thousands yearly.
